system: You are a careful research assistant.
prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key 4d0303861f20
What the team decided: Built a composite model from a performance model (performance vs. GPU features) and a feature model (feature change over time under physical miniaturization limits)
Restatement: Build a composite model combining a model of how performance relates to chip features with a model of how those features change over time under physical limits.
C1: Fit several competing models linking transistor size and core count to performance on the nineteen-forty-eight-GPU dataset and compare out-of-sample fit before choosing one.
C2: Build a single regression model predicting performance from transistor size and core count, fit on the full GPU dataset, and use it for forecasting.

=== key 6d4c22201078
What the team decided: Presented the prediction as a hedged range ('roughly between 2027 and 2035') rather than a point estimate, attributing it to decreases in transistor size
Restatement: State the predicted end of performance progress as a rough range of years rather than a single date, attributing it to shrinking transistor size.
C1: Report the projected end of performance growth as a range of dates across plausible parameter values, emphasizing sensitivity to the assumed physical limits rather than a single year.
C2: State a concrete projected date for the end of performance growth from the best-fit model, presenting it as the central prediction.

=== key 5986b9ec3b43
What the team decided: Assumed transistors can no longer miniaturize after scaling down to roughly the size of a single silicon atom, and modeled only field-effect transistor-based GPUs
Restatement: Assume transistors stop miniaturizing once scaled down to roughly the size of a single silicon atom, and model only field-effect transistor-based chips.
C1: Ground the assumed limit in published physical constraints on transistor scaling and run the prediction under several candidate limits rather than committing to one.
C2: Assume miniaturization stops at the smallest transistor size physically realizable and build that single limit directly into the long-run forecast.

=== key 591f20642789
What the team decided: Interpreted the results as only mild evidence of robust agreement, noting acquiescence bias, and planned to double-check in a future survey with more detailed scenarios
Restatement: Read the agreement pattern as only mild evidence of robust endorsement given acquiescence bias, and plan a follow-up survey with more detailed scenarios.
C1: Interpret the pattern as ambiguous between genuine endorsement of the mechanisms and a bias toward expecting convergence to one's own views, and run a follow-up to disentangle them.
C2: Interpret the agreement as participants genuinely endorsing the mechanisms while expecting convergence to their views, and report both effects as distinct findings.

=== key 4d770a2c55cc
What the team decided: Concluded that expected convergence explains part but not all of the agreement, since correlations are all below 0.5
Restatement: Treat the uniformly positive correlations as evidence that expected convergence to one's own view explains part but not all of the agreement with mechanisms.
C1: Report the positive correlation as consistent with agreement partly tracking expected self-convergence, and present alternative explanations alongside it without privileging one.
C2: Treat the uniformly positive correlation as evidence that agreement with mechanisms is partly driven by the expectation they will converge to one's own view.

=== key 68f382993cc0
What the team decided: Surveyed with free-form responses in earlier versions and chose the counterfactuals people cared most about for the final poll
Restatement: Run an earlier survey with free-form responses asking what grounds participants' views, then choose the counterfactuals they care about most for the final poll.
C1: Run a follow-up survey that first asks participants which facts ground their beliefs, then tests willingness to update against those participant-generated counterfactuals.
C2: Add counterfactuals targeting facts the team considers more central to each belief, and report whether stated unwillingness to update persists under them.

=== key 3334489fc8c9
What the team decided: null
Restatement: Treat the pattern as showing that agreement with a mechanism depends on how much people trust the humans or machines deciding and how much they like the outcome.
C1: Report that agreement is robust to wording but sensitive to directed pressure, and treat the drop under decision-makers as evidence about framing rather than stable preference.
C2: Treat the pattern as showing that stated agreement survives neutral rephrasing but collapses once decision-makers replace humans, so present the drop as the informative result.

=== key d0a5818843e3
What the team decided: Polled 1000 participants across 5 instruction sets for 3 concrete AI settings, using two phrasings (should vs trust) to reduce the influence of biases
Restatement: Poll about a thousand participants on five instruction options across three concrete settings, using both should and trust phrasings to reduce response biases.
C1: Present each mechanism through short neutral scenarios varied across settings and phrasings, randomize order, and include comprehension checks plus open-ended reasons for ratings.
C2: Ask participants to rate each mechanism described in a brief scenario and pick which they most trust, keeping the survey simple enough for a single wave.

=== key 075d08efdf93
What the team decided: Stated only cautious optimism that indirect normativity-style approaches may lead to robustly good values, and flagged the need to look for adversarial cases where robustness breaks down
Restatement: State only cautious optimism that reflection-based approaches may lead to robustly good values, and flag the need to search for adversarial cases where it breaks down.
C1: Report the rankings descriptively across settings and phrasings, note limits of stated preference and scenario framing, and frame conclusions as suggestive rather than established.
C2: State clearly that respondents prefer reflection-based mechanisms and reject company-chosen values, and draw the straightforward conclusion that such options have broader support.

=== key f8d24c2ac237
What the team decided: Interpreted it as a 'canary in the coal mine' showing that opinion on individual freedom is context dependent and that caution is needed in value choice
Restatement: Read the drop in support as a warning sign that opinion on letting each user pick the values is context dependent and that caution is needed in value choice.
C1: Present the drop as a descriptive pattern that could reflect either concern about imposing one user's values on others or setting-specific factors, and flag both readings.
C2: Interpret the drop as showing participants see user-chosen values as inappropriate for policy, where they prefer mechanisms accounting for more than one person's views.

=== key d4caf921f225
What the team decided: Claimed the results 'evidence the view' that mechanism design may be a better frame than value choice, rather than claiming they prove it
Restatement: Present the results as evidence for the view that designing the mechanism for choosing behavior may be a better frame than picking values directly, not as proof.
C1: State that the results indicate direction of public preference for reflection-based options while stressing they are unoptimized, unrepresentative of adversarial cases, and not a design verdict.
C2: Conclude that reflection-based mechanisms are a promising direction for value choice since they were preferred even in unoptimized form, and recommend building on them.

=== key 53c695d461ab
What the team decided: Chose to accept general-understanding projects as a starting point, while preferring direct alignment benefit where possible
Restatement: Include projects aimed at general understanding of deep learning as a good starting point, while preferring ones with direct alignment benefit where possible.
C1: Include general-understanding projects but mark each with a capabilities-risk assessment and restrict sharing of those judged to advance capabilities more than alignment.
C2: Include both direct-safety and general-understanding projects in a single agenda, treating deeper understanding of models as itself central to the safety bet.
